transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, Maestro Salieri! A pleasure to see you, though I confess I did not expect such an esteemed visitor today. Please, come in, come in. Forgive the dust, we are always quite busy here. How may I be of service? Though I must warn you, the Master Builder himself is away, visiting various lumberyards and craftsmen out in the countryside. He won't be back for several weeks, I'm afraid.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Good day to you. It is indeed a pleasure to visit your workshop, though I must say I am quite disappointed with the state in which my newly commissioned fortepiano has arrived. The keys stick, the pedal mechanism is faulty, and the upper register produces a thin and tinny tone. This is unacceptable. I demand that these issues be rectified immediately. The instrument must be in perfect working order for the Imperial Court's music room."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Maestro, that is most concerning to hear. A fortepiano with such issues is indeed a serious matter, especially for the Imperial Court. I assure you, quality is the cornerstone of our workshop's reputation.

However, as I mentioned, the Master is away. And... well, all commissions from this workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery and acceptance. The Court’s own servants, I recall, signed the receipt just last month, attesting to the instrument's good order upon arrival. Our guild rules, you see, strictly forbid reopening a completed commission without the Master’s personal approval. Without his direct instruction, I am simply not permitted to authorize any repairs or replacements. My hands are tied, I'm afraid, until he returns.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "I understand the constraints of your guild rules, but the quality of the instrument cannot be overlooked. It is unacceptable for an instrument bearing my name to be in such a state. The reputation of the Imperial Court's music room is at stake. I implore you to find a way to address these issues promptly. Surely there must be some protocol for urgent matters such as this. I cannot allow the Emperor's court to be subjected to inferior craftsmanship."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Maestro, I truly sympathize. Your concern for the Imperial Court's reputation is entirely understandable, and indeed, admirable. No one here wishes to see anything less than perfection associated with our work or with your esteemed name.

However, guild protocol is quite rigid, especially when it comes to completed commissions. "Urgent matters" typically refer to new requests or materials delays, not to instruments that have already been signed for and accepted. My authority, as the Master's journeyman, extends only to the day-to-day operations and preliminary discussions for *new* work. To reopen a completed commission, particularly one of such magnitude for the Imperial Court, requires the Master's direct and personal intervention. He is the only one with the discretion to make such an exception to the rules. Believe me, if there were any other way for me to assist you in this matter, I would. But without his return, which, as I said, will not be for several weeks yet, I am truly powerless.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I appreciate your adherence to guild protocol and your dedication to upholding the standards of your craft. However, the urgency of this matter cannot be overstated. The integrity of the Imperial Court's music room is of utmost importance, and we cannot afford to wait several weeks for the Master Builder's return. I trust that you understand the gravity of the situation and the implications of a faulty instrument in such a prestigious setting.

I urge you to consider all possible options to expedite the process of rectifying the issues with the fortepiano. Surely there must be a way to address this without violating any guild rules or causing undue distress. I implore you to find a solution that will ensure the swift correction of the instrument's deficiencies. The music of the court relies on the excellence of its instruments, and we cannot falter in our commitment to perfection.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Maestro, you speak with great passion, and I do grasp the weight of your words regarding the Court's music. It truly is a delicate matter. But you ask me to find a solution that bypasses the Master's authority, yet adheres to guild rules, and... well, those two things are often at odds in such a situation.

The *only* "option" I could conceivably offer, without violating my sworn duty to the Master and the guild, would be for you to perhaps... consider commissioning a *new* instrument. We could begin discussions immediately for a replacement fortepiano, one built to your precise, updated specifications. That would fall squarely within my purview. But to touch the existing instrument, the one already delivered and accepted... that remains strictly forbidden for me. I am truly sorry to be so unyielding, but I must protect the workshop's standing within the guild, and my own position here, until the Master returns. My apologies, Maestro.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
"Herr Schmidt, while I appreciate your dedication to upholding the guild's rules and your commitment to the workshop's reputation, I must insist that commissioning a new instrument is not a viable solution in this case. The custom fortepiano that was delivered to the Imperial Court was specifically crafted to meet the Court's requirements, and it is essential that this instrument be restored to its intended state.

I understand the challenges posed by the absence of the Master, but I urge you to consider the greater importance of honoring the commitment to quality and excellence that both the workshop and the Imperial Court represent. I cannot accept the suggestion of commissioning a new instrument as a replacement when the existing one can be rectified with the necessary repairs. I implore you to find a way, within the bounds of your authority, to address the issues that have arisen with the current fortepiano. The music of the Court depends on it."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Maestro Salieri, you are a persistent man, and I respect that greatly. And truly, I agree with you on the principle of quality and excellence; those are the very foundations upon which this workshop is built, and why our instruments are sought by the highest courts.

However, the specific fortepiano you refer to is, in the eyes of the guild, a *completed* commission, signed off upon delivery. My authority, as I’ve explained, extends to new work, to materials, to the training of apprentices. It does *not* extend to overriding a completed contract or a signed receipt. To do so would not only put my own position at risk, but it would also jeopardize the workshop’s standing with the entire guild. I simply cannot touch that instrument for repairs or replacement without the Master's explicit, personal directive.

The Master, he alone has the authority to make such a decision, to bend the rules for exceptional circumstances. And he, as I've repeatedly stated, is away for several weeks. There is no clause in my journeyman's charter, no secret instruction, that permits me to act on a fulfilled commission. I am truly sorry, Maestro, but my hands remain bound by the rules until his return. I can only offer to record your detailed complaints, with utmost precision, for the Master's review upon his eventual return.

"I understand your position and the constraints under which you operate, but I cannot help but feel deeply frustrated by this impasse. The musical integrity of the Imperial Court is at stake, and the imperfections in the fortepiano cannot simply be overlooked until the Master's return.
